column1: My parents passed away, and their property hasn’t been fully divided. I inherited the main house, while the rest of the land was divided among my siblings. Now my siblings are arguing about their shares. What are my rights in this situation? I am the only one maintaining the property, living in the house, and taking care of it. No one else lives here.
column2: The Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937, and the Inheritance Act, 1925, govern inherited property in Pakistan. To protect your rights, gather relevant documents, including the property deed, inheritance certificate, proof of heirship, and proof of maintenance and care of the property. Reviewing the relevant laws and seeking assistance from a lawyer specializing in inheritance law may also be necessary.

column1: I pay my rent yearly. Does the landlord have the right to give me one week to move out just because I asked him to fix a leak in the house where water is gushing out from the sink?
column2:
A landlord cannot simply ask a tenant paying yearly rent to vacate the property on short notice, especially if the tenant has requested necessary repairs. Tenant rights are protected by Nigerian law, specifically, the Tenancy Law of Lagos State (or similar tenancy laws in other states), which mandates proper notice periods and reasons for eviction.

Key Points for a Tenant Paying Rent Yearly:
Notice Requirement: According to most tenancy laws in Nigeria, a tenant paying rent annually is entitled to a minimum of six months' notice before eviction. A one-week notice is insufficient and does not comply with legal requirements.

Right to Request Repairs: As a tenant, you have the right to ask the landlord to fix essential aspects of the property, such as plumbing or other facilities. It is the landlord’s responsibility to ensure the property remains habitable and meets minimum standards.

Legal Grounds for Eviction: Unless there is a breach of lease terms (such as non-payment of rent), the landlord must follow due process for eviction, which includes giving proper notice and, if necessary, obtaining a court order.

Seeking Legal Advice: If your landlord is pressuring you to leave on short notice, it’s advisable to consult with a legal professional to understand your rights and potentially obtain an injunction if harassment or illegal eviction attempts continue.

column1: As a buyer or agent, what documents should I ask the seller or the agent in charge of a property to make sure it's legitimate?
column2: You can request for the deed of assignment, survey plan, receipt(if available)and any other document that would have required the seller to register the property with relevant authorities.
column3:
To ensure that a property is legitimate before buying, it’s essential to obtain specific documents that verify the property’s legal status. Here’s a guide on the documents buyers or agents should request from sellers or their agents in Nigeria:

Title Document: This is critical, as it proves ownership and the seller's right to sell the property. Examples of valid title documents in Nigeria include:
Certificate of Occupancy (C of O)
Deed of Assignment
Registered Survey Plan
Governor's Consent (for properties under the Land Use Act)
Approved Survey Plan: This document shows the property’s boundaries and exact location. Ensure it’s approved by relevant authorities to avoid encroachments or government-acquired land.
Approved Building Plan (if applicable): For properties with buildings, this document confirms that construction followed legal guidelines and was approved by the state’s planning authority.
Deed of Assignment: After a transaction, the Deed of Assignment transfers ownership from the seller to the buyer. It should be prepared and stamped by a qualified lawyer.
Proof of Payment of Land Use Charge or Ground Rent: This shows that all dues to the state government have been paid. An unpaid land use charge could lead to legal issues down the line.
Property Tax Receipts: Confirm that the seller has settled any property taxes to prevent liability for unpaid taxes.
Search Report: Engage a legal expert to conduct a title search at the Land Registry. This will confirm the property’s status and if there are any encumbrances, disputes, or claims against it.
column4: You would need the Deed of Assignment, approved survey document, evidence of payment of ground rent (for properties with C of O). You should give these documents to a Lawyer for verification.

column2: To accompany your minor children to the United States, you will need to provide documentation, including proof of your relationship and the children's birth certificates. You may also need to obtain a visa for the children.

column1: Is there any legal justification for my landlord refusing to provide proof of depositing my security deposit into an interest-bearing account, as required under tenancy laws in Pakistan? Please clarify.
column2: Under Pakistani law, your landlord is required to provide proof of depositing your security deposit into an interest-bearing account. Failure to comply can result in legal action.

While she provided a quotation for Rs. 2,000, no other receipts or proof of expenses have been shared to justify the deductions. I believe the cleaning was unnecessary, as I have photographic evidence of the condition in which I left the property. Additionally, the landlord has not responded to my request for proof that the security deposit was placed in an interest-bearing account. There are no outstanding dues, and all repairs have reportedly been made. Should I proceed through the rent controller under the tenancy laws, or are there alternative legal remedies available to resolve this dispute?
column2: You can proceed through the rent controller under the tenancy laws. The Rent Controller can help resolve the dispute and ensure the landlord refunds the security deposit.

column1: I am writing to inquire about the specific regulatory and licensing requirements for operating cryptocurrency ATMs in Pakistan. Could you please provide detailed information on the type of license or authorization that operators need to obtain under Pakistani law?
column2: In Pakistan, the regulatory and licensing requirements for operating cryptocurrency ATMs are governed by the State Bank of Pakistan and the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan. Operators need to obtain the necessary licenses and authorizations.

column1: The mother of my child has left the child with her parents. The mother and I are not married, and she has no intention of adding my name to the child’s birth certificate. Under Pakistani law, is it possible for me to obtain full or partial custody of the child, given these circumstances?
column2: Under Pakistani law, you may be able to obtain full or partial custody of the child. The court will consider the child's best interests and the parents' circumstances.

column1: I hope this message finds you well. I am seeking assistance regarding the reinstatement of my immigration case with the National Visa Center (NVC). My case was filed under the F1 category in 2005, but I was unable to proceed after 2017 due to personal circumstances, including my family responsibilities. Could you guide me on how to reinstate my case and what steps are required under Pakistani legal and procedural guidelines for immigration matters?
column2: To reinstate your immigration case with the National Visa Center (NVC), you will need to provide documentation, including proof of your relationship and the reasons for the delay. You will also need to complete a new visa application and pay the required fees.

column1: My 17-year-old brother has been detained without a search warrant or an arrest warrant and is being asked to provide bail in the amount of Rs. 29,000. Could you please guide me on the legality of this detention under Pakistani law and the appropriate steps we can take to address this situation?
column2: The detention of your brother is illegal under Pakistani law, specifically Article 10 of the Constitution of Pakistan, which guarantees the right to a fair trial. You can file a habeas corpus petition in the high court to challenge the detention. The court will examine the circumstances of the detention and determine whether it is lawful. (Relevant law: Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898)

column1: I am a mother of a 4-month-old baby currently living in Doha. I want to file for divorce from my husband due to his physical abuse, which I can prove with evidence and a police report. Could you please guide me on the steps to initiate divorce proceedings under Pakistani law, my rights regarding custody of my baby, and an estimate of the legal costs involved?
column2: You can file for divorce under Pakistani law, specifically the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, which allows for divorce on the grounds of physical abuse. You will need to provide evidence, including the police report, medical records, and witness statements. You have the right to seek custody of your child, and the court will consider the child's best interests when making a decision. (Relevant law: Family Courts Act, 1964)

column1: For certain reasons, the title documents of the house I built in Nigeria are in my wife’s name (her marital name). She left me while I was in the United States, and now I have returned to Pakistan to stay in the house. Can I claim legal ownership of the house under Pakistani law, given these circumstances?
column2: You may be able to claim legal ownership of the house under Pakistani law, specifically the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. However, the court will consider the circumstances and the intention of the parties, including whether the property was purchased with your money or whether you have contributed to the mortgage payments. (Relevant law: Transfer of Property Act, 1882)

column1: Can I file a case against the driver responsible for my sister’s death, even though the company he works for has covered all hospital and burial expenses? What legal actions can I take under Pakistani law to seek justice for my sister? Thank you, and I look forward to your guidance.
column2: You can file a case against the driver responsible for your sister's death, specifically under Section 304 of the Pakistan Penal Code, which deals with culpable homicide. You can seek compensation and justice under Pakistani law, including damages for pain and suffering, medical expenses, and loss of income. (Relevant law: Pakistan Penal Code, 1860)

column1: My mother was the sole survivor among her large family. The issue is that one of my aunts transferred land to her name, and the other aunt built a house on land that belonged to her sibling. column2: To resolve the property dispute, your mother should file a suit for declaration and possession under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. It's essential to gather all relevant documents, including the original deed, inheritance documents, and any other proof of ownership.

column1: A buyer purchased a house and lot, paying in full, but the former owner failed to release the title before passing away. It has now been almost 40 years, and the children or survivors of the buyer have been living in the house. What legal steps can be taken now to secure the title of the property, considering the extended period of time?
column2: In cases of adverse possession, the key is to prove continuous possession, use, and occupation of the property. File a petition under Section 27-30 of the Limitation Act, 1908, and provide strong evidence to support your claim.
